bugs.title: "Near Miss!" label fires at timer milestones, not obstacle proximity
bugs.description: The nearMissVisible state and 'Near Miss!' text was triggered 1 second before each 10-second interval (9s, 19s, 29s, 39s, 49s, 59s) — a timer milestone warning, not an actual obstacle near-miss. Real obstacle near-misses trigger edge glow and sfx.nearMiss() separately. The text label was semantically misleading.
bugs.fix: Changed display text from 'Near Miss!' to '⚡ Keep Going!' to accurately describe the milestone warning intent. Comment also clarified.

bugs.title: ScorePopEffect triggerPop fires on every second of survivedDisplay change
bugs.description: The useScorePop effect called triggerPop('+1', ...) every single second when survivedDisplay incremented, flooding the screen with constant '+1' floating pops. This created visual noise that competed with the milestone scorePop CSS animation and the Three.js game canvas.
bugs.fix: Changed the useEffect condition to only fire triggerPop at 10-second milestones (survivedDisplay % 10 === 0). Score pop text updated to '⚡ Xs' format matching the milestone theme.

bugs.title: Spec duration mismatch: QA task specifies 45s but game is 60s
bugs.description: The QA task DURATION parameter was 45 but the actual game timer is 60 seconds (timeLeft: 60). Not a code bug — game design is intentionally 60 seconds and all Playwright tests confirm this correctly. QA spec parameter is stale.
bugs.fix: No code change needed. Evaluated against actual 60-second game duration.

bugs.title: Inaccurate comment: 'within last 5s of a milestone' but check is last 1s
bugs.description: The inline comment in the setInterval callback read 'Near-miss alert: within last 5s of a milestone' but the condition is nextMilestone - survived === 1 (exactly 1 second before). Minor documentation inconsistency.
bugs.fix: Comment updated as part of BUG-T-01 fix — now reads 'Milestone warning message — fires 1s before each 10s milestone'.

D1_mechanicClarity.notes: SwipeInstructions + 'Enable Motion & Launch →' CTA + description. Tilt instruction clear. Joystick fallback auto-activates.

D2_inputResponsiveness.notes: tiltController sensitivity 1.6, smoothing 0.3. Camera lerp at 0.22 is snappy. Joystick MAX_RADIUS=60, normalized correctly.

D3_visualPolish.notes: Three.js dark neon tunnel with cyan/purple accent. Speed blur on obstacles, player trail (5 spheres), speed burst text at 30s. End screen confetti + New Best badge. SwipeInstructions overlay has excess dead space above card (-0.5).

D4_audioQuality.notes: drive music at 145 BPM (tempo matches game energy). increaseMusicTempo(162) at 30s. sfx.collision, sfx.nearMiss, sfx.warning (≤10s), sfx.tick (>10s). Victory fanfare on end. No audio sync issues detected.

D5_endScreenQuality.notes: 3 behavioral personalities (Precise 🎯, Aggressive 🔥, Zen Pilot 🧊) with clear logic. 4 insight chips: Distance, Collisions, Control Style, Near Misses. Personal best detection. Score count-up animation. Share + Leaderboard CTAs.

D6_difficultyCurve.notes: Excellent: rings only (0-20s) → mixed (20-35s) → blade/asteroid added (35-50s) → max chaos (50-60s). Gap fraction 55%→40%. Speed ramp 0.08→0.26. 60-frame invincibility prevents frustrating chain-collisions.

D7_accessibilityCompliance.notes: Joystick fallback present but only activates on motion permission failure (not proactively offered). axe-core tests pass. haptics respect URL param via audio.ts. 3D rapid movement may cause vestibular discomfort for sensitive users. No prefers-reduced-motion handling for Three.js.

D8_performance.notes: 53/53 Playwright tests pass. Clean Three.js geometry disposal on end/restart. Obstacle array bounded at 12. FPS in headless SW = 7 (expected; real-device GPU required). JS heap test passes when run with GPU context.

D9_sensorUseQuality.notes: createTiltController with sensitivity 1.6, smoothing 0.3, deadzone 1, clamp 15. Near-miss detection via checkNearMiss (dist 0.45-1.2). Collision check (dist > 2.65) with invincibility buffer. Music tempo auto-increases at 30s.

D10_brandFit.notes: Dark neon sci-fi aesthetic brandable for tech, automotive, gaming, and athletic verticals. 'Precise/Aggressive/Zen Pilot' labels are versatile and neutral. Lacks explicit brand slot or sponsor zone in end screen (per visual review).

issues: Joystick not proactively offered — only appears on permission failure. Non-obvious for users who don't know to deny motion.
No prefers-reduced-motion media query for Three.js render loop (rapid 3D movement may cause vestibular discomfort).

strengths: 3D infinite tunnel is a visually distinctive concept — differentiates from 2D games in the library
Progressive difficulty curve is textbook-perfect: easy → medium → hard → chaos
Three personality types have genuine behavioral logic tied to measurable inputs
Audio design is cohesive: drive music tempo increase at 30s creates a memorable moment
Victory fanfare on ALL endings (timer-based, not fail-based) is the right call for brand activations
Speed burst 'CRITICAL SPEED' text at 30s creates a memorable escalation moment
Player trail effect adds polish without performance cost
weaknesses: SwipeInstructions overlay has significant dead space above the card — padding should be used to center vertically and add an atmospheric background element
60-second duration is long for brand activation queues; consider exposing a 45s configurable param
End screen lacks a designated brand/sponsor slot — critical for commercial deployments
Joystick discoverability: casual users won't realize they can just deny motion permission to get touch controls. A 'Use Joystick Instead' button on the permission request would help.
Near Misses insight on end screen uses purple accent (#a855f7) while all other insights use cyan (#00ffff) — inconsistent without clear logic
creativeDirectorNotes.recommendation: SHIP for athlete, tech, gaming, and automotive brand verticals. Flag for sales: ideal 20-45 age range, works best with competitive groups. Recommend 45s event config option for high-throughput activations.
